bib.title: Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
bib.venue: IJCNLP-AACL 2023 (13th IJCNLP and 3rd AACL), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 305-329

question: Can chain-of-thought reasoning be made a faithful explanation of how the answer is produced, without losing accuracy?
hypothesis: Guaranteeing faithfulness by executing a symbolic reasoning chain with a deterministic solver does not cost accuracy and may improve it.
contributions: Faithful CoT: Translation (LM writes interleaved NL and symbolic chain) then Problem Solving (deterministic solver) so the chain is a faithful explanation
Generalises over multiple symbolic languages (Python, Datalog, PDDL, relational expressions) and 4 domains; new few-shot SOTA on 7 of 10 datasets
Analysis of ablations, exemplar and phrasing robustness, solver role, human plausibility study, error patterns

method.summary: Few-shot prompting of an OpenAI code LM to translate a query into a chain of NL subquestions (with dependencies and support rationales) interleaved with symbolic code; a Python interpreter, Datalog executor, PDDL planner or a CLUTRR transitivity-rule engine executes it to give the answer. Compared with standard, CoT and Least-to-Most prompting under greedy and self-consistency decoding on 10 datasets.
method.task: Few-shot reasoning: math word problems, multi-hop QA, planning, relational inference

metrics.name: Final-answer accuracy
metrics.definition: Exact match; MWP integers rounded to nearest integer; Boolean exact match for StrategyQA/Sports; SayCan plan correct if among gold plans; string exact match otherwise

metrics.name: Human-rated chain correctness
metrics.definition: Prolific annotators label chains with correct answers as correct, incorrect NL, incorrect SL, flawed question, confused; majority label; inter-annotator agreement reported

eval.protocol: Baselines rerun on cleaned test sets and with 10 exemplars (Wei et al. text says 10, appendix 6); no significance tests; exemplar-set and phrasing robustness give mean/std; human study: 100 chains per domain, >=3 annotators, ~100 annotators total, $16/hr, $280 cost; SayCan annotated by authors.

prompts.text:
# Q: There are 15 trees in the grove. Grove workers will plant trees in the grove today. After they are done, there will be 21 trees. How many trees did the grove workers plant today?
# To answer this question, write a Python program to answer the following subquestions:
# 1. How many trees are there in the beginning? (independent, support: ["There are 15 trees"])
trees_begin = 15
# 2. How many trees are there in the end? (independent, support: ["there will be 21 trees"])
trees_end = 21
# 3. How many trees did the grove workers plant today? (depends on 1 and 2, support: [])
trees_today = trees_end - trees_begin
# 4. Final Answer: How many trees did the grove workers plant today? (depends on 3, support: [])
answer = trees_today

# Context: [Jason] always had some great adventure planned for his granddaughter [Guillermina] when she came to visit. So, naturally, when [Myrna] told her daughter [Guillermina] that they would be going to visit [Jason] she could hardly contain herself.
# Question: How is [Jason] related to [Myrna]?
# To answer this question, we write a program to answer the following subquestions:
# 1. How is [Jason] related to [Guillermina]? (independent, support: "...")
relation(Jason, Guillermina) = grandfather
# 2. How is [Guillermina] related to [Myrna]? (independent, support: "...")
relation(Guillermina, Myrna) = daughter
# 3. Final answer: How is [Jason] related to [Myrna]? (depends on 1, 2)
relation(Jason, Myrna) = relation(Jason, Guillermina) @ relation(Guillermina, Myrna)

User query: Bring me something not sweet to eat.
Goal in PDDL:
(:goal
; I need to find a snack
(exists (?s - snack)
; it has to satisfy the following conditions
(and
; the snack must not be sweet
(not (is-sweet ?s))
; bring it to the user
(at ?s user)
)
)
)

limits: code-davinci-002 was discontinued on 2023-03-23, so part of the results cannot be replicated without continued access (authors' Limitations).
Only the Problem Solving stage is faithful; the Translation stage (how the LM writes the chain) stays opaque.
Faithfulness does not imply correctness; chains can be wrong yet faithful, and humans rated 66.7% of StrategyQA chains correct among correct answers.
NL comments matter little on GSM8K, Date, SayCan; roles left to future work; PAL/PoT matches it on 6 of 10 datasets (<2.0 difference) and is better on AQuA.
StrategyQA is worse than CoT (Datalog sparse in pretraining; knowledge retrieval is the bottleneck).
SOTA claims compare best-of-LM against published numbers from different models; baselines rerun on authors' cleaned test sets; no significance tests; all models closed OpenAI API, ~2022-23.
Human study used non-expert crowd workers; DataLog replaced by Scala for StrategyQA annotators, SayCan annotated by authors.
